newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Tatra truck output falls, loss seen.
newsitem.headline: Czech Tatra truck output falls, loss seen.

text.p: The troubled Czech truck maker Tatra a.s. said on Wednesday that it made 1,804 heavy utility vehicles last year, down from 2,014 in 1995, and falling short of its plan to make at least 2,000 units in 1996.

Tatra's spokesman Ivo Celachovsky told Reuters that the company again would post a loss for 1996, after a consolidated loss of 775 million crowns in 1995, but that specific results for last year were not yet available.
He said the company was planning to make 3,200 trucks this year, and swing to a 70 million crown net profit.
Complete results for 1996 will not be revealed until an audit is completed before the middle of this year.

Tatra is now owned by Czech conglomerate Skoda a.s. which acquired a controlling stake in the debt-ridden firm last year and made it a part of its growing engineering group, which also includes another truck maker, Skoda LIAZ a.s..
Tatra, during its peak production years, once produced up to 15,000 heavy-duty trucks per year, but production fell sharply after the 1989 end of communism.
Tatra also makes a small number of luxury limousines and light utility vehicles.
